svg.text: Formation of lymph
blood capillary (arterial end to venous end)
interstitial fluid between the cells
water, nutrients, hormones, gases, wastes, small proteins
leak out under capillary pressure; most returns to the
venous end, about 3 litres a day do not
lymph capillary
blind-ended; more permeable than blood capillaries,
so larger molecules enter too; the fluid inside is lymph
lymph capillaries join into lymph vessels (with valves), then the right
lymphatic duct and the thoracic duct, which open into the right and
left subclavian veins; skeletal muscles, moving viscera and breathing
keep the lymph flowing towards the thoracic duct
the lacteals of the villi are lymph capillaries that take up chylomicrons
A lymph node
several afferent vessels in
efferent vessel out
masses of connective tissue with lymphocytes; in the neck,
armpit (axilla) and groin; they filter the lymph, and their
lymphocytes and macrophages destroy bacteria and viruses
painful swelling (as in mumps) is mostly dead lymphocytes
and macrophages that have accumulated
Lymphoid masses
spleen, thymus, tonsils and adenoids, and masses in the
mucosa and submucosa of the gut; they make lymphocytes.
The spleen filters blood, destroys aged RBCs and stores RBCs.
Green: lymph. Red: blood capillary. The lymphatic system returns excess fluid and proteins to the blood and helps defend the body.
